bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the AK-pattern field strip as documented in Zastava’s own ZPAPM70 manual, which WBP’s own page says the WBP Jack shares. It is not WBP’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from WBP exists for this model, but WBP’s own page says the WBP Jack is built on the AK pattern, and that pattern’s take-down is documented by Zastava’s own ZPAPM70 manual. This guide follows it: confirm the pattern by sight, clear the rifle, then the classic five-part field strip. If what you see does not match a step, stop there and clean the rifle with the action locked open.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 7.62x39. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Confirm it is built the AK way
steps.action: Look for the pattern before you touch it: a long safety lever down the right side of the receiver, a sheet-metal dust cover with a round release button at its rear, and a charging handle fixed to the bolt carrier on the right. All three present, carry on; anything else, stop and clean the rifle with the action held open instead.

steps.title: Magazine off, safety down, handle back — look and feel, twice
steps.action: Press the magazine release lever and rock the magazine out. Move the safety lever down to FIRE — on this pattern the handle cannot come back with the safety up — then pull the charging handle fully rearward and look into the chamber and the receiver. Put a fingertip to the chamber. Ride the handle home under control, then do it all a second time.
steps.quote: Once determined that the chamber is empty, push down on the safety lever and let the bolt go back forward to home position.
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 3, pp.18-19

steps.title: Release button in, dust cover off
steps.action: Press the recoil spring’s release button — the serrated stub protruding from the rear of the dust cover — and lift the cover off from the back end.
steps.quote: raise the receiver cover from the back end with your other hand.
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 4, p.18

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out
steps.action: Push the recoil spring assembly forward until its base clears the receiver’s rear plate, lift it, and draw it out of the bolt carrier channel.
steps.quote: Lift the recoil spring cam and remove recoil spring assembly from the bolt carrier channel
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 5, p.18
steps.warn: USE PROTECTIVE EYEWEAR TO PREVENT EYE INJURIES!

steps.title: Carrier and bolt up and off the rails
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully back; when the carrier meets the rear of the receiver, lift it up off the rails and bring carrier and bolt out together.
steps.quote: Once the back of the bolt carrier contacts the back plate of the receiver, release pressure on the bolt cocking handle, this will allow the bolt carrier to move up and off the receiver rails.
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 6, p.19

steps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
steps.action: Turn the carrier over, rotate the bolt so its guide lug leaves the carrier’s channel, and draw the bolt out. Note how it sat; it goes back the same way.
steps.quote: Rotate the top of the bolt to the right and move it rearward with your right hand so that the guide lug on the bolt leaves the channel in the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 7, p.19

steps.title: Gas tube lever up, tube off — and that is the whole strip
steps.action: Rotate the gas tube’s locking lever clockwise to vertical and lift the gas tube with its upper handguard off the gas block. Five groups off — cover, spring, carrier, bolt, tube — and the strip is complete. The trigger group and the gas piston joint stay exactly as they are: WBP’s work.
steps.quote: Rotate the gas tube locking lever (see picture #16) clockwise, untill it’s in vertical position and gas tube is unlocked.
steps.cite: Zastava ZPAPM70 Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — Owner's Manual and Safety Instructions — SECTION 5.1 Field Striping, step 8, p.19
steps.warn: Use caution when ield stripping your irearm, as spring and other parts may become dislodged during disassembly process!

steps.title: Bore from the muzzle with a guide, chamber and bolt face wiped
steps.action: Brush the bore wet with solvent — from the muzzle with a rod guide so the rod never rides the crown, or a pull-through dropped in at the chamber — then dry patches until clean and a lightly oiled patch for storage. Wipe the bolt face, the carrier’s underside, the gas piston’s head and the inside of the receiver; carbon on the piston comes off with the brush, and the piston face is left dry.

steps.title: Oil sparingly where steel slides
steps.action: A thin film on the carrier rails, the bolt’s lugs and tail, and the charging-handle track. Nothing pours into the trigger group, and the gas tube goes back dry.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the receiver, the carrier, the bolt and the stock for cracks, a bent gas piston or a cracked cover, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for WBP.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until WBP has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the WBP Jack, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from WBP exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to WBP, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: From the muzzle with a rod guide, or a pull-through from the chamber
Brush wet with bore solvent, then dry patches until clean
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: CARRIER, BOLT & GAS
tasks: Carbon brushed off the gas piston, piston left dry
⛔ Nothing poured into the trigger group

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A thin film on the carrier rails and bolt lugs

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Gas tube first, lever back down
reassembly.action: Front end of the gas tube onto the gas block, rear end aligned with the rear sight base’s groove, pushed down until seated, and the locking lever rotated back flat.
reassembly.quote: Attach the gas tube assembly and upper handguard by holding the irearm with one hand, and install the front end of the gas tube on the gas block with other hand.

reassembly.title: Bolt back into the carrier
reassembly.action: Carrier upside down, bolt shaft into its guide hole, drawn fully rearward, guide lug into the channel and rotated until the bolt runs fully forward.
reassembly.quote: Insert the bolt shaft into the guide hole on the bolt carrier and bring the bolt fully rearward.

reassembly.title: Hammer cocked before the carrier goes in
reassembly.action: Look into the open receiver: the hammer must be cocked, locked under the sear. If it stands up, there is no room for the carrier.
reassembly.quote: Make sure that the hammer is cocked (locked underneath the sear) before attempting to install the bolt carrier!

reassembly.title: Piston into the tube, carrier onto the rails
reassembly.action: Gas piston into the gas tube’s mouth, carrier pressed down against the hammer spring until its grooves line up with the receiver rails, then run fully forward.
reassembly.quote: Insert the gas piston into the gas tube end (picture #19) and align the back face of the bolt carrier with the inside face of the back plate of the receiver.

reassembly.title: Recoil spring assembly back in
reassembly.action: Recoil spring retainer into the carrier channel, cam pushed forward, its lugs set in front of the grooves in the rear plate, then eased back until it locks.
reassembly.quote: Push the recoil spring cam forward, placing its guide lugs in front of the grooves, inside receiver’s rear plate.

reassembly.title: Dust cover on until the button springs out
reassembly.action: Front edge of the cover into its groove at the rear sight base, rear end pressed down until the release button pops out through its hole and holds it.
reassembly.quote: Install the dust cover. Insert the front edge of the cover into the groove in the back of the rear sight base.

fncheck: Magazine off and the chamber proven empty twice. Cycle the charging handle: the carrier runs fully back and returns fully to battery, and the safety lever moves cleanly between its upper and lower notches, blocking the handle when up. This check never asks you to pull the trigger.
